newsitem.title: USA: Expert says Simpson shown in same shoes as killer.
newsitem.headline: Expert says Simpson shown in same shoes as killer.

text.p: A 1993 photograph of O.J. Simpson showed him wearing shoes identical to those worn by the killer of the football star's ex-wife and her friend, an FBI expert testified at Simpson's civil trial on Wednesday.
As jurors watched closely, William Bodziak compared 18 features of the size-12 shoes seen worn by Simpson to a second photograph depicting a pair of exclusive Bruno Magli shoes.
"Based on all these features combined, I was able to determine that the shoe depicted in this photograph of the right foot of Mr. Simpson is a Bruno Magli Lorenzo shoe," he said.
Simpsonis expected to testify on Friday for the first time about his whereabouts on the night of the murders when he is to take the stand in his civil trial. He did not testify in the criminal trial.
During his deposition to lawyers in preparation for the civil trial he said he would never own such a pair of "ugly- assed" shoes.

Simpson was acquitted in October 1995 of the June 12, 1994, murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ronald Goldman. He is fighting a wrongful death civil lawsuit filed by the victims' families.
Bodziak told the jury that only 299 pairs of size 12 Bruno Magli Lorenzo shoes were sold in the United States between 1991 and 1993.

Bodziak testified during Simpson's criminal trial that the killer wore size 12 Bruno Maglis, but the photo of Simpson -- taken in Buffalo during a football game where Simpson was working as a TV analyst -- did not surface until this year.
Defence attorneys were expected to argue that the picture, taken by a freelance photographer, was doctored.
Earlier in the day a limousine driver testified there was no sign of Simpson at his mansion at the approximate time plaintiffs' attorneys argued the murders were committed.

Allan Park, who drove Simpson to the airport that night for a flight to Chicago, told jurors he saw a 6-foot (1.8-metre), 200-pound (91-kg) black man entering Simpson's darkened mansion at 10:54 p.m. A moment later the lights came on.
Simpson has said during a sworn deposition and in interviews he was the person Park saw in the driveway, but maintained he had been home all night.

Plaintiffs' attorneys tried to establish the murders were committed at about 10:35 or 10:40 p.m. and maintain Simpson had time to kill Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald Goldman outside her townhouse and return to his mansion two miles away, where he was spotted by Park.
Defence lawyers contended Simpson could not have commited the murders, disposed of bloody clothing and the murder weapon and got back to his mansion in time to meet the limousine.

Testifying for the plaintiffs, Park told jurors he arrived at Simpson's Brentwood home about 10:23 p.m. and did not see Simpson's white Ford Bronco parked in front. But he later conceded under cross-examination he was not looking for parked cars.

He said he rang the bell at the gate repeatedly during the next 30 minutes and got no response until he saw Simpson's house guest, Brian "Kato" Kaelin, walking across the driveway, with Simpson appearing seconds later.

Park also said he saw a small black bag in Simpson's driveway but when Kaelin offered to put it in the limousine trunk, "Simpson jumped out and said, 'No, no, no, that's OK, I'll get the bag, don't worry about it, I'll get it.'"
Park said that after Simpson picked up the bag, he never saw it again. The plaintiffs' attorneys suggested the bag contained bloody clothes and possibly the knife used in the murders.
